# Matic Execution Plan
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

Next action: run Measure against the reconciled implementation for issue #53 (Feat: make active user status more obvious and prevent accidental access revocation).

## Outcome And Boundary

Issue #53 (Feat: make active user status more obvious and prevent accidental access revocation) requires the administrator Members page to make active access clear and make revocation deliberate. Source: https://github.com/adventistasia/lead-lab/issues/53.

The correction is limited to the existing Members page presentation and confirmation flow. It may update `application/source/resources/js/pages/admin/members/index.tsx` and its focused test carrier after Design confirms the current test organization. Reuse existing UI primitives where possible.

The work must not change account-state classification, the revocation or restoration endpoint, server authorization, role behavior, member data, activity-log semantics, routes, schema, external services, infrastructure, production configuration, or historical records. Revoked users keep the existing single-click restoration path.

## Sequence

1. Define the bounded outcome, acceptance conditions, and human Continue checkpoint.
2. Design: inspect the current active and revoked member-row actions, available dialog primitives, server action contract, local runtime, and existing feature or frontend test carriers. Confirm whether any target-environment or ownership input blocks local implementation.
3. Build the smallest UI correction: a clear active-state indicator, non-destructive active-user revoke styling, a confirmation dialog with synthetic member name and email plus the access consequence, and a second-click confirmation that calls the existing action. Preserve cancel, escape, focus, and restore behavior.
4. Add focused regression coverage for active and revoked states, confirmation content, no action before confirmation, confirmed revocation, restoration, authorization, and responsive presentation as supported by the repository test setup.
5. Capture `evidence/active-revocation-confirmation.png` from local synthetic `.test` data. Check the image for real participant data, credentials, cookies, tokens, private URLs, and other sensitive content before publication.
6. Reconcile source, tests, run evidence, PM Control records, and deployment guidance if affected. Measure all acceptance conditions and the quality rubric before Learn or Publish.

## Verification And Rollback

- Run the focused member/access feature tests selected during Design.
- Run the full supported PHP suite and frontend checks applicable to touched paths, including TypeScript, lint, formatting, production build, and `git diff --check`.
- Manually verify the active state, revoke confirmation, cancel path, keyboard dismissal and focus, confirmed revocation, revoked-user restore, and no horizontal overflow at representative mobile and desktop widths using synthetic accounts.
- If checks fail, revert only the issue-specific application and test changes. No migration, endpoint, authorization, deployment, or production change is planned.

## Controls And Handoffs

ISS-25 (Active administrator member status and revocation controls are visually ambiguous) and ACT-85 (Implement and verify safer administrator member revocation controls) track this work. CHG-46 (Separate administrator member lists by account state) and RQ-09 (Administrators must approve, grant, revoke, and restore participant access) provide the approved access-management boundary. RQ-08 (The application must work on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices), RQ-10 (Protected routes, APIs, and files must enforce server-side access controls), and RQ-15 (The application should support participant, moderator, and administrator permissions) remain applicable. No new human-only decision is required for the bounded local correction. DEP-10 (Gate 1 environment and ownership evidence for credible staging and production planning) remains open; no staging deployment or production change is authorized.
